Lotus's official model history identifies the 2-Eleven production period and six-speed transmission; the service notes identify its clutch hardware.

claims.basis: Lotus's official model history identifies the 2-Eleven production period and six-speed transmission; the service notes identify its clutch hardware.

Lotus specifies a six-speed transmission. The standard car uses a conventional driver-operated manual transaxle; no sequential or paddle actuation is documented. Downshift-only action. Modeled only for upshifts. Lotus documents a driver-operated clutch assembly on the standard car, so the clutch is required to launch from rest. The 2007 standard-car cockpit image shows a continuous circular three-spoke rim. The fully visible wheel has no integrated display; the instruments are mounted in the dashboard. No wheel-mounted shift-light strip or lamps are visible on the fully exposed wheel face. The photographed rim forms a continuous closed circumference rather than an open-top wheel.
